subject: Acme RAG eval - post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme RAG eval - post-call recap and next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps while it's fresh: 

Recap
- Goal: Improve grounding and reduce hallucinations for Acme's legal Q&A assistant across 10k documents (policies/contracts/internal memos).
- Current baseline we reviewed: large LM + simple BM25 retriever; grounding rate ~62% on the sample set; hallucination concerns around citation fidelity.
- Key success criteria (confirm): >80% grounding_rate at top-1, <8% hallucination on prioritized prompt set, avg latency (95th) <800ms for 1-2 concurrent users.

Recommended evaluation plan (short list)
1) Models to test (initial):
   - redwood-clarity-7b (fp16) — strong instruction-following, good tradeoffs for latency/cost.
   - llama2-13b-chat (q4) — larger context/window for multi-doc reasoning; test in our dedicated infra.
   - redwood-instruct-3b (quantized) — low-cost baseline for throughput-sensitive paths.

2) Retrieval & reranker suggestions
   - Embeddings: text-embedding-3-large (512d) for initial vector store.
   - Chunking: 600 token chunks, 100 token overlap (legal doc heavy).
   - Retriever: hybrid (BM25 + bi-encoder) with bi-encoder top_k=20, then cross-encoder rerank top_k=5.
   - Reranker: cross-encoder-reranker-v1 (recommended) — best for citation precision on legal text.

3) Metrics & monitoring to include in the eval harness
   - Grounding_rate@1 (percentage of responses with correct doc citations at top1)
   - Hallucination_rate (annotated false assertions per 100 responses)
   - EM_precision@1 (exact-match precision for short factoid answers)
   - Latency p95 (generation + retrieval + rerank) and cost per 1k requests

Artifacts & links
- I've uploaded the summary PDF and sample prompt set (attached). Full benchmark page: https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/benchmarks/acme-rag-2026-03-20.html
- Sample prompt set highlights the prioritized question types we agreed on.

Questions I have for you
- Are the success criteria above aligned with Acme's priorities? (especially the grounding target)
- Can we get a stable sample of ~500 queries + truth labels from your side so we can run an apples-to-apples baseline?

Proposed next steps
- Technical deep-dive with Ethan (retrieval) + Logan (infra/ops) — suggested slots: Wed 24 Mar 10am PT or Thu 25 Mar 11am PT.
- We'll run an initial 3-model benchmark in our sandbox with your sample labels and share results within 5 business days after receiving data.

Attachments: acme_rag_eval_summary_20260320.pdf, sample_prompt_set_v2.md, retriever_config.json

Thanks — I'll hold Wed 10am PT for now; confirm if that works.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme RAG eval - post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Reranker latency/cost: the cross-encoder looks promising for precision, but we worry about added latency and cost per query. Can you share an expected latency delta and rough cost estimate for the bi-encoder+cross-encoder hybrid you suggested?

2) top_k values: we currently expect most user questions to be short; would lowering the bi-encoder top_k to 10 and reranking top5 still be defensible? We want to optimize for latency while preserving grounding quality.

3) Data: we can share the 500-question sample and labels by EOD Monday.

4) Deep dive: Wed 24 Mar 10am PT works for me — please send calendar invite.

Also please attach the sample prompt set and the benchmark page (I couldn't open the S3 link from my network).

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Product Manager, Search & Assistants | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme RAG eval - post-call recap and next steps

Alex — great, thanks for the quick replies and for confirming Wed 24 Mar 10am PT. Calendar invite sent. Quick answers inline: 

1) Reranker latency/cost: for our infra, cross-encoder reranking of top5 adds ~120-250ms on top of retrieval + generation depending on model choice (redwood-clarity vs llama2-13b). Cost delta vs bi-encoder-only is roughly 2.5x on the reranking portion but since we only rerank a small set it's usually <15% increase in per-request cost for the hybrid approach. I'll include a short cost model in the meeting notes.

2) top_k tuning: lowering bi-encoder top_k to 10 is reasonable for shorter queries and will reduce end-to-end latency; I still recommend re-ranking top5 for citation precision. We'll include an ablation in the benchmark (top_k 10/20 and rerank 3/5) so you can see tradeoffs.

3) Data ingestion: thanks — once we receive the labeled 500 queries we'll run the initial benchmarks in the sandbox. We'll also run an internal check for label coverage and edge cases.

4) Next actions before Wed:
   - You: share the 500-question sample + labels (EOD Mon) and any document access details.
   - Us: run a quick sanity baseline (bi-encoder top_k=20, rerank top5) and share the summary PDF and a short Loom with key failure modes within 5 business days after data receipt.

Attachments (re-attached): acme_rag_eval_summary_20260320.pdf, sample_prompt_set_v2.md, retriever_config.json

I'll also add Ethan and Logan to the invite; they'll prepare a short section on retriever configs and quantization options. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Marissa
